observation_summary: The application throws an UnsupportedOperationException when performing operations involving varargs, such as argument capturing or constructor instantiation, indicating that the internal logic for handling these variable-length arguments is either incomplete or incorrectly implemented.
reasoning_summary: The widespread UnsupportedOperationException across various Mockito features (varargs, constructor instantiation, stubbing) suggests that the internal method logic responsible for processing these inputs is failing to handle the specific data structure of varargs correctly. This is a procedural failure in the implementation of the argument-handling algorithms, rather than a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: Bug report title: ArgumentCaptor no longer working for varargs
evidence_gaps: The specific code snippet containing the throw statement is not provided, but the symptom is characteristic of an unimplemented or incorrectly implemented method path.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the exception suggests a missing capability, it is likely a procedural implementation gap within existing methods rather than a missing design-level class or object.
The error is not a missing guard or validation check, but rather a failure in the execution of the core logic for handling varargs.
